title: Inter Miami pays tribute to Lionel Messi’s father, Jorge, after his death
content:
Inter Miami paid tribute to Lionel Messi’s father, Jorge Messi, after he died on Saturday following an illness. He was 68.

Miami was hosting Liga MX’s Monterrey at Nu Stadium in the Leagues Cup, with Lionel Messi absent as he traveled home to Rosario, Argentina, to be with his family. Messi had been training with the team as recently as Friday. During the World Cup, Messi’s family had indicated in a statement that Jorge was undergoing treatment for a “health situation.” Lionel was visibly emotional at times during Argentina’s run to the World Cup final, saying after his hat trick in his team’s opening match vs. Algeria that his tears were due to “something unrelated to football” after “a few difficult, complicated days.”

Messi’s MLS club held a minute of silence before Saturday’s match for Jorge, who also served as Lionel’s agent and business manager and confidant throughout his career and helped oversee his move from PSG to Miami in 2023.

Miami players also wore black armbands to honor their captain and his family. Messi’s close friend and international teammate, Rodrigo De Paul, captained the squad in his absence. Around Nu Stadium, fans held messages and signs of support for Messi as well.

Tributes for the Messi family poured in throughout the day from around the soccer world, with clubs — including Messi’s Argentine youth team, Newell’s Old Boys, and Barcelona, where he rose to prominence — the Argentina federation and South American confederation among the many writing messages and offering condolences.

Barcelona, which faced Nottingham Forest in a preseason friendly on Saturday, also observed a prematch moment of silence out of respect.

MLS commissioner Don Garber shared a statement of condolence as well, writing, “We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Jorge Messi. Jorge will be remembered for his quiet strength, kindness and unwavering devotion to his family. On behalf of Major League Soccer, we extend our heartfelt condolences to Lionel, the entire Messi family and all who loved Jorge. We are keeping them in our thoughts during this difficult time.”

It’s unclear when Messi, who scored his first two goals since the World Cup and added an assist in Miami’s Leagues Cup win over Atlético San Luis on Wednesday night, will return to the club. Entering Saturday, he was the all-time leading scorer in the Leagues Cup (14 goals; tied with LAFC’s Denis Bouanga) and the two-time reigning MLS MVP. After leading Miami to an MLS Cup title last season, he’s one off the league’s golden boot pace with 12 goals, and, just over halfway into the regular season, has Miami in contention for the Supporters’ Shield that comes with the league’s best record.
